title: fix(chat): adopt Reactor preview.16 session-switch crash workaround
body:

Related: #1424

**Merge HOLD.** Published head `801f5ce01ebf8e4a98f0ca78d101cf0bd1d9a601` was rebased onto `main` snapshot `46062f01511d43c08fd541a6297e2479348a165a`, after [#1898](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1898) (chore: update Windows App SDK to 2.6.4). Required local unit suites pass and CI attempt 2 is green, but full-product native proof remains incomplete. **The exact upstream invalid-anchor sample crashes with preview.15; preview.16 completes twelve replacements on the same old native SDK and current SDK 2.6.4 Debug/Release.** This verifies the reduced mechanism, not complete Companion acceptance. **Strict final-marker clipping remains reproducible before the upgrade and without Reactor.**

## What Problem This Solves

<!--

Adopts the published Reactor mitigation for native chat session-switch crashes while preserving pooled accessibility and tooltip metadata.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.

-->

User impact: native chat uses the upstream recycled-anchor workaround alongside Windows App SDK 2.6.4 inherited from main. A local, unpushed test repair removes a selection-automation race; slow cycles and clipping remain unresolved. No new production scrolling fix is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Both Reactor packages move from preview.12 to `0.1.0-preview.16`, still the latest on both authoritative NuGet feeds. Package commit `459f7234dc2b0b72125f833ba86c051a554c12cf` includes [microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor#1214](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/pull/1214). Reactor's recycled-container workaround and native WinUI anchor safety address different parts of the failure.

The production delta is the package project plus three chat files, not a scrolling redesign:

| Compatibility change | Why the version bump needs it |
| --- | --- |
| Move the Markdown factory to Advanced and remove the preview.12 list callback | Advanced owns the wrapping Grid layout. The old callback expected a horizontal stack and would throw for the new shape. Sanitization, parser flags, inert links/images and block presentation remain application-owned. |
| Welcome alignment, HelpText and ToolTip use tracked modifiers | Preview.16 reports `REACTOR_POOL_001` for direct writes inside `.Set(...)`. Reactor must track these properties so reconciliation and pool reset update or clear them. |
| Timeline/composer use `.ItemStatus(...)` | Preserve accessibility and fixture observations without stale pooled metadata, analyzer suppression or disabling pooling. |
| Drawing moves from 10.0.11 to 10.0.12 | Meet Reactor's dependency minimum. |

The unchanged published nine-file delta is 161 insertions / 49 deletions. It does not import [#1449](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1449) (improve(chat): remove an unnecessary wait when opening chat history), replace `StartBringItemIntoView`, or add extent-driven retries.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

**Original invalid-anchor mechanism:** the exact source from [microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor#1213](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/issues/1213), SHA256 `D8ED327C3704B56153D9791C932DD5F60D4BF3290BB8EB538D20AD95F88F31F7`, starts a native bring to item 76 of 77, then immediately replaces keyed history through Reactor state. It has no OpenClaw, Gateway, Markdown, explicit collapse, forced layout or correction timer. Three separate package variants share this unchanged source:

| Reactor / native SDK | Configuration | Recorded result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| preview.15 / SDK 2.4.0 | Debug | First replacement failed; uninstrumented native exit `0xC000027B`. |
| preview.16 / SDK 2.4.0 | Debug | 12/12 selected-history transitions; driver 0, clean app exit 0. |
| preview.16 / SDK 2.6.4 | Debug | 12/12 selected-history transitions; driver 0, clean app exit 0. |
| preview.16 / SDK 2.6.4 | Release | 12/12 selected-history transitions; driver 0, clean app exit 0. |

The preview.15/preview.16 old-SDK outputs contain byte-identical native WinUI DLLs matching the original report's version, isolating the Reactor change from the SDK upgrade. A separate read-only observer run recorded bring return, state replacement/render, then unhandled `ArgumentException`, HRESULT `0x80070057`, `Handled=false`, and native exit `0xC000027B`. An additional native-debugger run resolved `ScrollingAnchorRequestedEventArgs::AnchorElement`, `ItemsView::OnScrollViewAnchorRequested`, and `ScrollPresenter::EnsureAnchorElementSelection` through `ArrangeOverride`, matching the invalid-anchor path in [microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#11865](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/issues/11865). This is not exact equality with the original full Measure-path stack. The debugger itself failed in its exception callback during detach; its `c0000005` is not an app access violation, and that run's STILL_ACTIVE receipt is not the uninstrumented crash-exit evidence.

These are reduced-mechanism checks, not full Companion/Gateway scheduling, sustained-stress or final-tail acceptance. Visible selected-history rows were verified in two successive UIA samples after each transition, not an independent compositor fence or measurement of native pending-operation duration. All nine attempts, including early runner/cleanup defects, are retained. Historical driver hashes distinguish the passing helper from the later failed-window-preserving helper. Sources, receipts, stack logs and owned-window captures are local artifacts, not public proof links.

**Pre-upgrade clipping control:** a separate, uninstrumented Release build uses the pre-upgrade chat sources from `46062f0` and core/Advanced preview.12, Drawing compile dependency 10.0.11, SDK/WinUI 2.6.4 and the unchanged scroll controller. Archived source Git blobs match after LF/CRLF normalization. Both Reactor DLLs match official package payloads; package archives match the NuGet catalog SHA512. Separate output/intermediate directories and a fresh synthetic Gateway profile were used, without simultaneous builds or UI runs.

The identical standalone UIA probe completed twelve natural-tail switches, then failed on the **third narrow resize** after the original single 0%/100% scrollbar sequence per width. The END marker remained clipped for 20s. The inspected owned-window image shows the final message's first paragraphs, but its final marker below the composer. A second 100% request recovered it only as a diagnostic after failure. This proves the strict symptom can occur before the upgrade, not that every failure shares a cause or that preview.16 cannot add another regression.

**Reactor-free native control:** a separate unpackaged Release ARM64 diagnostic uses SDK/WinUI 2.6.4, native `ItemsView`, `StackLayout`, `AnnotatedScrollBar`, ordinary TextBlock fixture rows, and the current `VerticalAnchorRatio=1` configuration. There is no Reactor package, Markdown renderer, Gateway, application reconciliation or extent correction. In resize-only mode ItemsSource never changes. Both traced and scroll-event-tracing-disabled runs established the natural final marker, qualified the first 900/1300-width pair, then clipped the END marker on the second narrow resize for twenty seconds after the original single 0%/100% sequence per width. Actual window widths and transcript-width changes greater than 200 physical pixels were measured; qualifying visibility required two successive UIA samples. Inspected owned-window captures show message240's heading with the final marker below the composer.

The traced control ended at offset `35456.5674`; a subsequent extent increase raised the maximum to `35499.4275` without another view adjustment, leaving about 43 DIPs unscrolled. The trace-disabled run ended at scroll `99.879265%`. These diagnostic builds have different recorded hashes because the event-subscription gate was added between them, not a same-binary A/B. A later unchanged untraced instance failed its initial natural-tail precondition before any switching/resizing; that failure is retained, not a passed stress control. **This establishes that the endpoint failure mode can occur without Reactor under the tested native configuration. It does not establish identical causality for every product failure or exclude additional upgrade regressions.** Sources, receipts and captures are retained locally, not represented as public artifact links.

**Application lifecycle trace:** a trace-only preview.16 build captured an extent increase after the final `ViewChanged`, without another offset adjustment. Suppressing resize-triggered chat-width state updates still reproduced clipping on the third narrow resize; other reconciliation activity was not eliminated. Two extent-driven bring prototypes were rejected: one blocked during a pending initial bring; the guarded variant conflicted with explicit scrolling and failed its first narrow pass. No application crash or layout-cycle exception was established by either prototype. Neither entered repository production source.

The pinned [upstream parking fixture](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/blob/459f7234dc2b0b72125f833ba86c051a554c12cf/tests/Reactor.AppTests.Host/SelfTest/Fixtures/ItemsViewParkingFixtures.cs) explicitly separates fixed-height exact-end checks from variable-height estimated-extent behavior. This is supporting context, separate from the native control above, and is not proof of framework-only ownership of every application failure.

<details>
<summary>Retained executions, failures and comparison limits</summary>

| Execution | Actual result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Initial Debug fixture | Profile/app 32/32; UI 19 passed / 13 failed / 0 skipped. Final marker clips after widening from 900x720 to 1300x950; stress reached 7/12 before its 150s watchdog. Other failures included fixture `projects.list` rejections, activation, an MCP-token file-sharing error and a rejected blank capture. |
| Initial Release | Profile/app 32/32. Full UI produced no completed TRX before 10 minutes, then output-pipe capture failed. Partial evidence retained; exact owned leftover app stopped. Not a passed suite. |
| Focused Release | 4 passed / 1 failed / 0 skipped. Both-width tail, fractional voice, late-history isolation and populated pages passed; stress failed in `SelectSessionAsync` with a test-side NRE before cycle output. |
| Mounted Debug | 14/14 passed, zero skipped: Markdown, disposal, welcome metadata, composer observation and queued-message lifecycle. Not the full proof pool. |
| Earlier local harness repair | Expanded Debug profile/app 32/32 and UI 30 passed / 2 failed (`projects.list` cases). Its target stress/tail cases passed. Focused Release 2/2 passed. The runner's accidental expanded selection is retained, not relabeled a focused pass. |
| Final reviewed harness | Debug 2/2 passed: 12 cycles in 14.222s, tail in 13.743s. Release 0/2: wide-tail timeout, stress 7/12 in 152.215s including cleanup, about 21s/cycle. App responding; no selector NRE or native layout-cycle exception. |
| Subsequent ordinary Release, unchanged test DLL | 2/2 passed: 12 cycles in 15.000s, strict tail in 7.044s. Earlier 0/2 retained. An external CPU sampler failed serializing its own final receipt after the test runner completed; completed TRX and runner output remain. |
| Independent ordinary preview.16 UIA instances | Twelve natural-tail switches succeeded. Original scrollbar/resize sequence clipped on third and first wide pass respectively, outside xUnit. One capture ends at message 238, with 239/240 offscreen for 20s. A second 100% diagnostic recovered one instance but failed in the other. Neither is acceptance. |
| Other diagnostics | Instrumented test-source copy 2/2, max measured UIA call 347ms: diagnostic only. Resize-only control stopped after 14 pairs on stale UIA. Suppressed-width control observed 50 pairs without independently qualifying settled rendering; not acceptance. Its scrolled-up control failed to establish the early marker. Inactive/attempted covered-window probes did not reproduce slow cycles; foreground qualification was refused. No foreground/occlusion cause established. |

[Build and Test 40720588483, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/40720588483) failed while disposing the fixture after the question-recovery test: Shared 4,665 passed / 8 skipped / 1 failed, aborted WebSocket/transport read. The stack ends in `FixtureGatewayServer.DisposeCoreAsync`, not a failed question assertion. CI Gate failed and revocation recovery E2E was cancelled. Hosted UI succeeded, but does not replace custom acceptance. Relevant published fixture sources match the frozen main snapshot; no independent main execution proved that CI failure baseline or flaky. [CodeQL 40720588401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/40720588401), including actual Actions/C# analysis, passed.

**CI follow-up, 2026-10-29:** attempt 2 **passed**, including CI Gate, after one `gh run rerun 40720588483 --failed --repo openclaw/openclaw-windows-node`. The fresh Core job passed Shared 4,666 / 8 skipped, Connection 1,694 / 1 skipped and WinNode CLI 129 / 0 skipped. The exact newly uploaded TRX confirms `Interactive_QuestionRecoveryAcrossSocketsAndResolutionBroadcast` passed in 151ms. Fresh revocation-recovery E2E passed 1/1 against the recorded Gateway 2026.10.8. Both fresh jobs checked out merge `dd5991ccae058caa6bbc833bdc57c0908809a420`, combining unchanged head `801f5ce0` with base `46062f01`. Previously successful jobs, including hosted UI, were reused, not rerun. This confirms the original shutdown failure is intermittent on that unchanged candidate; it neither tests the local repair nor clears custom stress/scrolling acceptance.

**Latest local follow-up, 2026-10-29:** the receive loop now treats an `OperationCanceledException` as expected only when its connection is cancelled or its socket is already Aborted/Closed, matching the existing WebSocket exception filter. Responder failures are still awaited separately; the expanded guard preserves the exact unowned cancellation exception as well as `InvalidOperationException`. This is an uncommitted test-support repair, not production behavior or a hosted-CI result. The original question-recovery test passed 100/100 locally before the repair, so its original timing was not reproduced. A new faithful real-WebSocket regression now reads a partial synthetic 32MiB response, pauses its reader through the existing fixture peer, and requests restart. The original receive filter fails disposal with `OperationCanceledException: Aborted`, inner transport IOException/SocketException 995 and the same receive-to-disposal stack; the repaired filter passes. All 101 protocol tests then passed, including both exact responder-fault guards. This proves the shutdown boundary with real backpressure, not the original question scenario's exact interleaving. The regression costs about five seconds because it exercises the fixture's existing restart deadline, with no new timeout, process, desktop or exported seam.

One new phase-timed Release diagnostic completed 12/12 cycles. It did not reproduce the retained four-second gaps: the largest measured call was a 429ms tree lookup; activation, dropdown expansion/collapse and MCP history reads stayed below 40ms. An uninstrumented control then passed both original cases, with twelve cycles totaling 14.158s and the strict both-width tail test passing. Earlier failures remain retained, and slow-cycle attribution remains unresolved. The diagnostic and control used the unchanged frozen Release app and existing Release fixture dependencies; they do not prove the new receive filter. Ordinary UI tests were force-recompiled afterward and instrumentation absence checked, rather than assuming an incremental build restored them. All three new app identities and both fixture-process identities were verified absent; all 602 frozen runtime hashes still match.

A subsequent diagnostic removed per-call filesystem pacing by buffering timings in memory and flushing after the bounded test. It also completed 12/12, with the largest measured call 407ms; it does not explain the earlier slow instance. Separate same-binary native anchoring controls were inconclusive: bottom and top anchoring failed the initial natural-tail precondition before any resize pairs, and the disabled-anchor run failed its process-identity precondition before UI observations. An earlier runner attempt failed while recording its source inventory. Those attempts are retained as failures, not qualifying comparisons or a proposed configuration fix. The last identity failure was subsequently traced to `Process.MainModule` reporting `ntdll.dll`, not proven PID reuse. A fresh audit against the intended executable and creation time confirmed the process absent. The session-only runner now uses the native executable-image query, requires the expected image, and checks creation time before PID-reuse handling. A controlled non-UI child verified expected-image qualification, preservation of a deliberately stale identity and exact-owned cleanup. Ordinary UI test instrumentation was removed again, the original 602-file app runtime still matched, and the desktop was released for the separately owned cron proof.

[CI 40728085479 at ff1ca7f, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/40728085479) used x64 Debug, preview.12 and SDK 2.6.4. It shares 30 cases with this PR, but **does not run the twelve-cycle stress case**. Its 31 cases add a question scenario; this PR's 32 add stress and a fixture guard. The published `GatewayFixtureUiTests.cs` files are identical before the local repair, but production UI differs. Its 28 failures were 25 unexpected `question.list` cleanup assertions, 1 width delta of 900 to 1044 (less than 200), and 2 stream-visibility timeouts. Its geometry failure and question-recovery panel are not this PR's wide-tail assertion. Protocol/hosted geometry repairs remain separately owned.

Historical [31fff448 results/images](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1549#issuecomment-6370840331) and [e28 clipping captures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1549#issuecomment-6370357997) remain relevant negatives/limits, not current-head acceptance. Earlier 31fff448 Debug/Release completed 12 cycles in 22.871s/21.150s; slow stress is not consistent. Public links were verified.

</details>

**Local repair and review:** four uncommitted test-only files now differ. The two UI-test files retain the successful selector lookup instead of repeating a nullable search, inspect already-enumerated elements, and add timings/metrics; the fixture server and protocol test add the shutdown filter, real-socket regression and exact responder-fault guard above. Twelve cycles, the 150s watchdog, natural-tail checks and exact width/visibility assertions remain. Only optional metrics catch `ElementNotAvailableException`, outside actions/assertions. Independent rubber-duck review found no blocking UI helper defect and supported the preview.12 proof classification. Follow-up independent rubber-duck review checked the native-only and original-overlap sources, hashes, receipts, stack/observer logs and upstream report: no blocking evidence flaws or overclaims found. That review verified evidence integrity, not an independent rerun or full-product acceptance, and predates the new fixture repair. Whole-tree shared autoreview remains blocked by the previously documented canonical installation/authentication issue, not reported clean.

All failed attempts remain recorded. The original invalid-anchor path is now reproduced in the reduced sample; exact full-product scheduling, clipping ownership across every application failure, and slow-cycle attribution remain unresolved. The normal-source forced Release rebuild passed; the frozen original DLL/PDB were then restored. A fresh read-only audit on 2026-10-29 confirms **all 602 original runtime file hashes match** and no task-owned process remains among all 20 recorded overlap app/driver/debugger identities, including runs missing cleanup files: 19 PIDs absent, one reused by an unrelated process and untouched. Native-only app/driver cleanup was previously verified; the desktop reservation is released. No production source, commit, push, merge, runtime install, display setting or #1449 edit changed during this follow-up. The observed live `main` tip is now `5daead32131b9b0a7b90dd11ad98ced6da147d61`; these results remain tied to the recorded candidate, not claimed as a fresh rebase or combined-tree acceptance.

One further native diagnostic explicitly switched to short history after loading and then back to long history before attempting resize. The short marker qualified, but the long final marker did not become visible within the unchanged 20-second stage limit, so **zero resize pairs ran** and no anchor alternative was accepted. This run recorded 3,638 view/extent events while long history was active, with repeated offset/extent changes. That describes an unsettled diagnostic state, not an attributed Companion crash or proof of a scrolling fix. The screenshot and source/binary receipt were retained, both owned processes were verified absent, and the desktop was released. The corrected driver's independent non-UI checks accepted the expected image and creation time, rejected wrong-image and stale-time manifests, and left its helper alive until exact-owned cleanup.

A separately verified upstream lead is [microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#12085](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/issues/12085) and its still-open fix [microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml#12086](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/pull/12086): a non-animated bring after content reset can be clamped against stale compositor bounds even when UI-thread extent is current and `ScrollCompleted` reports completion. This is a matching failure class, **not attribution of the local clipping or slow cycles**. The upstream patch also explains why simply enabling animation is not a valid ItemsView workaround: [the virtualizing viewport forces animation off for an anchor outside the realized range](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/blob/main/controls/dev/Repeater/ViewportManager.cpp#L630-L637). No production animation, retry, anchor or timing change was adopted.

An observer-only follow-up now captures the native request/completion mismatch directly: long-history bring correlation 3 requested offset **34,522** with scrollable height 34,621; its `ScrollCompleted` event arrived **5.879s later at offset 0**, with scrollable height still 34,619. This happened before app closure, not just during teardown. The final marker remained absent through the 20-second stage limit, so no resize pairs ran. The observer adds only request-event logging; its native WinUI DLL matches the preceding control byte-for-byte, the independent driver is unchanged, and both owned processes were verified absent. The SDK does not expose a public completion-result property here, so the event is not labeled a success result. This directly shows that completion is not tail arrival in this native, Reactor-free control; it does not independently inspect compositor bounds or attribute every Companion failure. The upstream reset/bring lead was already noted earlier and is reconfirmed, not a newly discovered framework issue.

Two further bounded controls did not supply a safe workaround. The first valid disabled-anchor run used the same app and driver hashes as the bottom-anchor baseline; it also failed long-tail arrival at offset 0 before any resize pairs. An ordinary `ScrollView.ScrollTo` variant used the identical native SDK DLL and unchanged driver, but still failed the final-marker precondition: completion offset 34,002 lagged scrollable height 34,997, and the final observation was 97.296% with no final marker. Both failures are retained, all owned processes were verified absent, and the desktop was released. No production anchor or navigation change was adopted. Cancelling native bring and substituting another scroll operation was not implemented: [current upstream ItemsView bookkeeping requires the original correlation's completion before releasing its retained target](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-xaml/blob/main/controls/dev/ItemsView/ItemsView.cpp#L1053-L1107), so a different operation cannot be assumed equivalent or safe.

Supplemental session-only native diagnostic commands: `dotnet build .\App\NativeItemsViewProbe.csproj -c Release --no-restore -v:quiet` and `dotnet build .\Driver\NativeItemsViewDriver.csproj -c Release --no-restore -v:quiet`, both passed with zero warnings/errors after the final diagnostic edits. `.\Run.ps1 -Mode resize-only` failed on second narrow resize with tracing; `.\Run.ps1 -Mode resize-only -WithoutEventTrace` also failed on second narrow resize. `.\Run.ps1 -Mode switch-resize -WithoutEventTrace` failed its initial-tail precondition before cycles began. These are local diagnostic executions from a separate artifact directory, not repository test counts or proof-pool passes.

The optional `-p:Platform=ARM64` adds an output segment causing 260-character SVG copy failures. Successful commands omit that optional segment, retaining the ARM64 RID; no copied-asset workaround or weakened assertion.

Supplemental original-source diagnostic executions, from the separate overlap artifact directory: `.\Run.ps1 -Variant p15-sdk24 -Configuration Debug` failed the first replacement with native exit `0xC000027B`; `.\Run.ps1 -Variant p16-sdk24 -Configuration Debug`, `.\Run.ps1 -Variant p16-sdk264 -Configuration Debug`, and `.\Run.ps1 -Variant p16-sdk264 -Configuration Release` each completed 12/12 transitions with driver/app exit 0. All four app configurations built with zero warnings/errors. The observer run `.\Run.ps1 -Variant p15-sdk24-diag -Configuration Debug` separately captured unhandled HRESULT `0x80070057`; the debugger run `.\Run.ps1 -Variant p15-sdk24 -Configuration Debug -CaptureCrashStack` supplied the anchor-setter stack, with the debugger failure and STILL_ACTIVE limit described above. These are retained reduced-mechanism executions, not new repository tests or complete proof-pool acceptance.

Earlier full and focused selections used these exact commands with the same explicit app/profile settings. Their results and incomplete attempts are retained in the execution table above:

```powershell
$profileFilter = 'FullyQualifiedName~GatewayFixtureProfileTests|FullyQualifiedName~GatewayFixtureRunTests|FullyQualifiedName~GatewayFixtureAppTests'
```
